audit.title: Supported Networks (Chainlink Automation)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The page opens with a shutdown callout and token-transfer prose, not a canonical statement. There is no liftable sentence answering "which networks does Chainlink Automation support?" A summary list/table at the top would fix this.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 32 sections, median 105 words, max 220, 0 over 600, consistent H2 (chain) → H3 (network) hierarchy.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong. 179 numerals, 40 hex identifiers, explicit gas limits and premiums per network. Minor: 0 numerals carry inline units (bytes/gas/LINK), so a value lifted out of table context loses meaning.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only 5 markdown links, 0 to primary sources. No links to the Automation architecture/registry concept pages or to contract source; explorer links are buried inside JSX props, not citable references.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The Parameters section defines each field crisply with its on-chain identifier (`paymentPremiumPPB`, `checkGasLimit`) — genuinely liftable. But core terms ("upkeep," "Registry," "Registrar") are used undefined.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `datePublished`/`dateModified`, no og/twitter tags. For a config page whose values change, a visible last-updated signal matters most. (Head metadata could not be verified from source — CLI should pass raw `<head>`.)

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks (acceptable for a reference table), but the addresses agents most need are wrapped in `<Address contractUrl="…0x…">` components — the value is only recoverable by parsing the URL, not from a clean labeled field.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what are the parameters" and per-network values well. No heading phrased as the actual query ("What networks does Chainlink Automation support?"), no note on the shutdown status in text.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent. Lone vague quantifier "fast gas feed" is an accepted technical term, not fluff.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured reference page: 20 clean per-network tables, 32 headings, no level skips, and dense concrete parameters (gas limits, payment premiums, contract addresses). Its single biggest strength is machine-scannability of the data. Its biggest opportunity is **answer-first extractability and address parseability** — the page never states, in a liftable sentence, *which* networks are supported, and the registry/registrar addresses live only inside `<Address>` JSX components, so a plain-text extractor sees URLs rather than clean `0x…` values. Combined with zero JSON-LD/canonical/date metadata, this good page under-punches for retrieval and agent consumption.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first supported-networks summary
recommendations.issue: No liftable sentence naming supported networks; page opens on token-transfer prose.
recommendations.change: Add one sentence + a summary table: "Chainlink Automation is supported on 11 networks: Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, Ethereum, Gnosis, OP, Polygon, Scroll, and ZkSync (mainnets and testnets)." Follow with a compact table of network → mainnet/testnet availability.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a single self-contained chunk to answer "which networks are supported," the page's implied primary query — currently answerable only by scanning 20 headings.

recommendations.title: Surface contract addresses as plain text
recommendations.issue: Addresses live only inside `<Address contractUrl="…0x…">`; text extractors get URLs, not values.
recommendations.change: Ensure the rendered output emits the literal `0x…` address as visible text in the cell (e.g. `` `0x37D9…891D1` `` alongside the explorer link), so a skim/parse yields a clean labeled address per network.
recommendations.why: Agents completing "get the Automation Registry address for Base" need a parseable value; a URL-only representation risks wrong or truncated extraction.

recommendations.title: State Automation shutdown status in text
recommendations.issue: Shutdown notice is a component with no fallback text; retrieval sees nothing.
recommendations.change: Add a plain-text sentence stating the shutdown status, effective dates, and migration guidance with an inline link, so engines don't answer from stale priors that Automation is fully live.
recommendations.why: An unretrieved status this material produces confidently wrong answers; a liftable sentence defends against it.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical, and a visible last-updated date
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, a self-referential `canonical`, and `inLanguage`; render a visible "Last updated" line. Config values change, so freshness is a trust signal.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness raise E-E-A-T and parse reliability for agents deciding whether these addresses are current.

recommendations.title: Add inline citations to canonical concept pages
recommendations.issue: Only 5 links, 0 to primary sources; terms like Registry/upkeep undefined.
recommendations.change: Link `paymentPremiumPPB`, `Registry`, and `checkUpkeep` to the Automation architecture/concepts pages and, where possible, to the on-chain contract source.
recommendations.why: Inline links to canonical definitions raise citation rate and let engines resolve entities correctly.

recommendations.title: Add units to parameter values
recommendations.issue: 179 numerals, 0 with inline units; a lifted "5,000" loses meaning.
recommendations.change: Label column headers with units — "Maximum Check Data Size (bytes)", "Check Gas Limit (gas)", "Payment Premium % (PPB basis)" — so a cell extracted alone is unambiguous.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims with units survive out-of-context extraction; unitless numbers are ambiguous to engines.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/query-phrased heading
recommendations.issue: No heading matches how devs ask ("what networks…", "what is the registry address for X").
recommendations.change: Add an H2 "What networks does Chainlink Automation support?" over the summary table from P1.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present.

antiPatterns: Address values hidden inside JSX component props with no plain-text fallback — impairs agent extraction.
Undated content on a page of mutable config values (no visible last-updated).
Callout components (`shutdown`, token-transfer notice) may render no extractable text — material status invisible to retrieval.
No keyword stuffing, fluff, or unresolved cross-references — clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; verify it lists this page.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templating likely governs the missing metadata here — fix at the docs-platform layer, not just this page.
CLI could not capture `<head>`; pass raw head HTML for a definitive metadata read before treating schema as absent.
